item.title: Cassandra Wilson Led Jazz Into the Future With Warmth and Creative Conviction
item.description: With a self-possessed vision, the vocalist married her easy and intimate tone to jazz, blues and folk experiments, opening the door to a new postmodernism.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Russonello
item.media:credit: Brian Harkin for The New York Times
item.media:description: Cassandra Wilson performing at the Rose Theater at Lincoln Center in 2011.

item.title: Mundane Amtrak Data Becomes an Ensemble Performance in Train Jazz
item.description: Train Jazz captures and maps the choreography of the Amtrak network into a seven-instrument jazz ensemble, now playing on an internet-connected device near you.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Nazaryan
item.media:credit: Heritage Art/Heritage Images, via Getty Images
item.media:description: Jazz big bands, like the one led by Cab Calloway, bottom right, often traveled by train to their performances.

item.title: Haruomi Hosono, Architect of Japanese Pop, Pushes West
item.description: After recent endorsements from Vampire Weekend and Harry Styles, Haruomi Hosono, 79, returns to the U.S. with a new album and tour.
item.dc:creator: Ben Sisario

item.title: Who Owns Reggaeton’s Beat? A Judge Throws Out One Claim.
item.description: A copyright suit against stars including Bad Bunny and Daddy Yankee came from the producers behind a trio of songs foundational to the genre.
item.dc:creator: Ben Sisario
item.media:description: Lawyers for Bad Bunny successfully challenged a judge’s earlier ruling in the case.

item.title: Miley Returns Without the Cyrus, and 8 Other Songs to Hear Now
item.description: Miley Cyrus wants to dance, underscores revels in hyperpop jump cuts, the producer Dahi enlists Kendrick Lamar and more.
item.dc:creator: Jon Pareles
item.media:description: Miley returns with the new single “Bass Persuades.”

item.title: 33 Albums and Shows We’re Looking Forward to This Fall
item.description: Some of pop’s highest-wattage stars (Charli XCX! Sombr!) hit the road, and artists including Riley Green, Miranda Lambert and Victoria Monét prepare anticipated new releases.
item.dc:creator: Elena Bergeron, Marcus J. Moore, Jon Pareles, Hank Shteamer, Ben Sisario, Harry Tafoya and Lindsay Zoladz
item.media:description: Charli XCX will tour in support of her LP “Music, Fashion, Film,” released in July.

item.title: Marian Anderson’s Ambition Was Always Clear: To Be a ‘Fine Artist’
item.description: Anderson’s importance as a barrier breaker in classical music has sometimes overshadowed the power of her artistry.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Tommasini
item.media:description: Marian Anderson, around 1935.

item.title: Rogers Stadium in Toronto Is Damaged by Thunderstorm Before AC/DC Show
item.description: The music venue, which opened in 2025, was built specifically for large concerts. The fate of its next show, featuring AC/DC, is unclear.
item.dc:creator: Alena Cerro and Amy Graff
item.media:credit: Keito Newman/The Canadian Press, via Associated Press
item.media:description: Rogers Stadium in Toronto, which opened last year to host large concerts, was damaged when a storm tore across the area on Wednesday. No injuries were reported.

item.title: Gene Bertoncini, Jazz Guitarist Who Dazzled With Subtlety, Dies at 89
item.description: He performed at the highest level for decades, sensitively backing singers like Tony Bennett and Lena Horne when not leading his own innovative groups.
item.dc:creator: Will Friedwald
item.media:description: Gene Bertoncini in 1999. He worked with many of the greatest jazz singers of the 20th century.

item.title: Burning Man Draws an Older, Wealthier Crowd, Data Shows
item.description: Last year, just one in 10 festivalgoers was in their 20s, according to researchers. A decade ago, the same group represented nearly 30 percent of attendees.
item.dc:creator: Neil Vigdor
item.media:description: Only one in 10 attendees at the Burning Man festival was in their 20s, according to researchers.

item.title: Lizzo Wants to Write a Great American Novel
item.description: But first, she’s publishing a children’s book, “Lil Lizzo Meets Sasha B. Flootin,’” because “I wanted to inspire young people to fall in love with music.”
item.category: Lil Lizzo Meets Sasha B. Flootin (Book)

item.title: Cassandra Wilson, Star Jazz Singer, Dies at 70
item.description: With a low and smoky voice, she conjured the blues tradition of her native Mississippi in both her own songs and in covers.
item.dc:creator: Will Friedwald and Adam Bernstein
item.media:credit: Hiroyuki Ito for The New York Times
item.media:description: Cassandra Wilson in 2014. In concert, she moved from Joni Mitchell to Muddy Waters to Hank Williams to Antonio Carlos Jobim to Bob Marley to her own imaginative compositions.

item.title: Patrick Gleeson, Who Made Synthesizers Part of Jazz, Dies at 91
item.description: He abandoned a job teaching college English in the 1960s to become a pioneer of the instrument, playing onstage with Herbie Hancock’s jazz band.
item.dc:creator: Alex Williams

item.title: Gary Glitter Pleads Not Guilty to Child Sexual Abuse Charges
item.description: Accusations against the glam rock singer relate to incidents that are said to have occurred between 1978 and 1981.
item.dc:creator: Alex Marshall
item.media:description: Gary Glitter in 2015.

item.title: Federal Judge Dismisses Lawsuit Against Lizzo and Her Touring Company
item.description: The singer, who has faced several lawsuits asserting harassment, discrimination and a hostile work environment, has repeatedly denied wrongdoing.
item.dc:creator: Alena Cerro
item.media:description: The case dismissed on Tuesday was filed regarding Lizzo’s 2023 tour.

item.title: Despite Duane Davis’s Conviction in Tupac Murder Trial, Some Still Seek Closure
item.description: When a man was found guilty of orchestrating the murder of Tupac Shakur, it brought catharsis to many who knew the rapper. But questions remain even after the trial.
item.dc:creator: Julia Jacobs and Jonathan Abrams
item.media:description: Tupac Shakur’s death after a drive-by shooting 30 years ago turned him into a pop cultural martyr and changed the trajectory of hip-hop.

item.title: Jason Isbell and Others Say Suno’s A.I. Imitates Their Voices
item.description: Jason Isbell and three others filed a lawsuit against Suno, accusing the company of training its model on their songs. The suit will test a legal strategy not based on copyright but unlawful imitation.
item.dc:creator: Ben Sisario
item.media:description: Jason Isbell, a Grammy-winning singer-songwriter, is a plaintiff in the lawsuit.

item.title: A Daisy Chain Fields Soundtrack
item.description: Hear tracks performed by Chappell Roan, Bikini Kill, Doechii and, of course, Olivia Rodrigo.
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Zoladz
item.media:credit: Amanda Hakan for The New York Times
item.media:description: Bikini Kill

item.title: At 70, Yo-Yo Ma Is Modeling a Way to Be in the World Today
item.description: With a global audience, Ma models a way of being that goes against the grain of cynicism, polarization and isolation. It’s up to us to pay attention.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Barone and Benjamin Rasmussen For The New York Times
item.media:description: “If we had nine or 10 Yo-Yos, the world would look different,” said the pianist Emanuel Ax, Ma’s longtime friend and collaborator.

item.title: Duane Davis Is Convicted of Orchestrating Tupac Shakur’s Murder
item.description: Duane Keith Davis, 63, was found guilty of first-degree murder after he went on an interview tour discussing his role in the 1996 drive-by shooting.
item.dc:creator: Julia Jacobs and Anusha Bayya
item.media:description: Duane Keith Davis, right, and his lawyer, Michael Sanft, after a jury found Mr. Davis guilty. He faces up to life in prison.

item.title: Who Is Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis, Convicted in Tupac Shakur Murder Trial?
item.description: Duane Keith Davis, once a high-ranking member of the South Side Compton Crips, long said he was in a Cadillac with the shooter in 1996. Then he began to recant his accounts.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Abrams
item.media:description: Duane Keith Davis was convicted of murder in the 1996 shooting death of Tupac Shakur.

item.title: Tupac Shakur Was at His Cultural Peak When He Was Killed
item.description: Shortly before he was murdered in 1996, the rapper had released “All Eyez on Me,” a landmark album that turned him into a superstar.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Abrams
item.media:description: Tupac Shakur performing in Milwaukee in 1994.

item.title: Here’s the latest.
item.dc:creator: Julia Jacobs

item.title: Closing Arguments at Tupac Shakur Murder Trial Focused on Suspect’s Statements
item.description: Duane Keith Davis was accused of orchestrating the drive-by shooting of the rapper in Las Vegas in 1996.
item.dc:creator: Julia Jacobs and Anusha Bayya
item.media:description: A lawyer for Duane Davis told jurors that his client’s account was like the movie “Titanic” in that it may have been based on a historical event, but the core plotline was made up.

item.title: Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Breaks Record With 20th Week at No. 1
item.description: The singer-songwriter set the record for a non-holiday song, topping the Hot 100 in a week that saw country hits dominate and Dolly Parton’s return.
item.dc:creator: Ben Sisario
item.media:description: Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas” has held the No. 1 spot on Billboard’s Hot 100 chart since February.

item.title: Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields: A New Feminist Music Festival Takes Shape
item.description: At the first Daisy Chain Fields festival, the 23-year-old pop star presented a cross-generational vision of female empowerment. (With Taco Bell activations, too.)
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Zoladz and Amanda Hakan
item.media:credit: Amanda Hakan for The New York Times

item.title: At the Tupac Trial, Old Rumors Still Trail Sean Combs
item.description: Duane Davis, who is charged in the murder of the rapper Tupac Shakur, repeatedly accused Mr. Combs of being behind it. He now says he was lying.
item.dc:creator: Julia Jacobs and Anusha Bayya
item.media:credit: Ron Galella/Getty Images; MEGA/GC Images, via Getty Images

item.title: Dolly Parton’s Marriage to Carl Dean Was Fueled by Distance and Difference
item.description: Dolly Parton met Carl Dean outside a Nashville laundromat in 1964. For decades, she was as protective of her marriage as he was fiercely private.
item.dc:creator: Derrick Bryson Taylor

item.title: Sarah Davachi’s Music: A Manifesto for Listening Closely
item.description: Sarah Davachi’s “The Will of Tongues” is a collection of music that refuses extremes and requires undivided attention.
item.dc:creator: Hugh Morris
